raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Give `sampling_params.flat_logprobs` a wire format on `/inference/v1/generate`: in tokens mode the choice carries `flat_logprobs`, three base64 `.npy` arrays of shape `[num_tokens, k + 1]` (token ids, logprobs, ranks; the sampled token in column 0), instead of one object per candidate in `logprobs.content`. Tokens-mode requests without stop strings also stop detokenizing, since nothing in that response carries text, and `FlatLogprobs.append_fast` extends its lists instead of appending element by element. Independent of #62342; the two touch neighbouring lines of the same serving method.

## Claims

- With the default single API server, `logprobs=8` or `logprobs=20` with `flat_logprobs=true` runs at the same throughput as `logprobs=0` on R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B, Qwen3-4B and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct: 2.0 to 2.8x main at k=8 and 4.1 to 5.4x at k=20, two trials each with no overlap.
- API-server CPU per generated token at k=8 with `flat_logprobs=true` falls 4 to 5x (95–105 to 21–25 µs with one API server, 64–79 to 18–23 µs with eight) and the response is 2.7x smaller (447 to 166 bytes per token; 975 to 360 at k=20).
- The `logprobs.content` shape is unchanged for clients that do not set `flat_logprobs`; those requests still gain 64 to 113% at k=8 on one API server from the detokenization skip and the container change.

## Validation

Same load and server flags as #62342: 768 chat-templated prompts from `sail/Sanity-Test-R1D-1.5B`, 256 in flight, `max_tokens` uniform in 128–1024, temperature 1, `top_p=0.95`, `top_k=512`, `vllm serve <model> --dtype bfloat16 --max-model-len 4096 --logprobs-mode processed_logprobs --generation-config vllm --max-logprobs 20 --return-sampling-mask --enable-scale-out --api-server-count {1,8}`, one H100 and 11 CPUs per job, main vs this branch in the same venv, two trials each. Client: [bench.py](https://github.com/AmineDiro/vllm/blob/assets/logprob-responses/logprob-responses/bench.py) with `--flat-logprobs`.

`/inference/v1/generate`, generated tokens/s, main → this PR ("flat" sends `flat_logprobs=true` to both servers, which on main only changes the engine container):

| model | API servers | k=0 | k=8 | k=8 flat | k=20 flat |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B | 1 | 16.9k → 20.7k | 6.8k → 14.4k | 7.8k → 21.7k | 3.8k → 20.2k |
| Qwen3-4B | 1 | 13.6k → 14.9k | 6.6k → 11.8k | 7.1k → 14.4k | 3.5k → 14.3k |
| Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct | 1 | 13.4k → 15.7k | 6.9k → 11.2k | 7.4k → 15.7k | 3.7k → 15.6k |
| R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B | 8 | 23.4k → 23.2k | 21.9k → 22.8k | 22.3k → 22.5k | 21.8k → 22.3k |
| Qwen3-4B | 8 | 14.9k → 15.0k | 14.3k → 14.5k | 14.4k → 14.7k | 14.3k → 14.5k |
| Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct | 8 | 15.7k → 16.2k | 15.4k → 15.5k | 15.6k → 15.4k | 15.2k → 15.6k |

![flat throughput](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AmineDiro/vllm/assets/logprob-responses/logprob-responses/flat_throughput.png)

API-server CPU, µs per generated token, main → this PR:

| model | API servers | k=0 | k=8 | k=8 flat | k=20 flat |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B | 1 | 33 → 22 | 111 → 41 | 95 → 21 | 227 → 23 |
| Qwen3-4B | 1 | 44 → 29 | 116 → 54 | 105 → 25 | 243 → 30 |
| Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct | 1 | 41 → 26 | 107 → 48 | 98 → 21 | 221 → 26 |
| R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B | 8 | 30 → 20 | 78 → 35 | 64 → 18 | 122 → 20 |
| Qwen3-4B | 8 | 37 → 24 | 92 → 42 | 79 → 23 | 145 → 24 |
| Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct | 8 | 33 → 23 | 80 → 37 | 68 → 21 | 130 → 23 |

<details>
<summary>CPU, response size and profile figures</summary>

![flat API CPU](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AmineDiro/vllm/assets/logprob-responses/logprob-responses/flat_api_cpu.png)

![flat bytes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AmineDiro/vllm/assets/logprob-responses/logprob-responses/flat_bytes.png)

py-spy on the single API server at k=8, R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B, sampled µs per generated token by category (first matching frame from the leaf; GC pauses are charged to the allocating frame):

![profile](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AmineDiro/vllm/assets/logprob-responses/logprob-responses/profile.png)

</details>

Tests: a new unit test of the arrays in `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_tokens_logprobs.py` and a new server test in `test_serving_tokens.py` comparing `flat_logprobs` with `logprobs.content` at temperature 0; the existing generate, stream, derender parity, `return_tokens_as_ids`, chat and completion logprob tests pass on one H100; `tests/test_logprobs.py` and `tests/v1/engine/test_logprobs_processor.py` cover `append_fast`.

## Details

With `logprobs=k`, main builds `k + 1` `Logprob` dataclasses per generated token on every step, decodes each candidate's text, keeps all of them alive until the request finishes, then builds a pydantic object per candidate for the response. py-spy on a single API server at k=8 puts 40% of its time in the response build and 20% in the per-step objects and decoding, which is why `logprobs=8` costs 50–60% of throughput there.

- `FlatLogprobs` (behind `sampling_params.flat_logprobs`, added for the GC overhead of `list[dict[int, Logprob]]`) already stores a request's logprobs as primitive lists, but nothing served it: `ServingTokens` indexed it per position, which rebuilds the dicts. The new `flat_logprobs` choice field serializes those lists directly as `.npy` arrays, like `routed_experts` and `prompt_token_id_logprobs` do on the same endpoint. Every position has exactly `k + 1` entries in the engine's layout (sampled first, then the top-k, which repeats the sampled token when it ranks there), so the arrays are 2-D and need no offsets; `logprobs.content` deduplicates that case, the one shape difference. Values are the engine's float32, not clamped, so `-inf` survives. In a stream the arrays are per chunk.
- Only `output_mode="text"` needs detokenized output, and stop strings need it in both modes; a tokens-mode request without stop strings now gets `detokenize=False`, the per-request form of what `--tokens-only` forces server-wide. That removes the per-candidate `convert_ids_list_to_tokens` and the incremental detokenizer for those requests. Requests with stop strings keep both.
- `append_fast` extends the four lists instead of appending in a Python loop; `islice` keeps the zip truncation it replaces.

After this, the single API server's largest remaining cost at k=8 is the msgpack decode of the sampling-mask arrays (40% of its time), not logprobs.

With `output_mode: "text"`, they are `ChatCompletionLogProbs` carrying the decoded token strings and their UTF-8 `bytes` for the sampled token and every entry in `top_logprobs`; a server started with `--return-tokens-as-token-ids` returns `token_id:N` placeholders there instead, as `/v1/completions` does.
 
+### Flat logprobs
+
+With `output_mode: "tokens"` and `sampling_params.flat_logprobs: true`, every choice carries `flat_logprobs` instead of `logprobs`: `token_ids`, `logprobs` and `ranks`, each a base64-encoded `.npy` of shape `[num_tokens, k + 1]` (int32, float32, int32). Column 0 is the sampled token, then the top-k in rank order, which repeat the sampled token when it ranks among them (where `logprobs.content` lists it once). The logprobs are the engine's float32 values, not clamped, so `-inf` stays `-inf`; a rank of 0 means the engine reported none. With `stream: true`, each chunk's arrays cover its own tokens, and a chunk with no tokens (the finish chunk after an abort) carries `null`, so the chunks concatenate along axis 0. The server builds these straight from its internal buffers, so a request with `logprobs: 8` or `logprobs: 20` costs about what `logprobs: 0` does; the object form is several times more expensive per token.

+import httpx
+import numpy as np

+    },
+).json()["choices"][0]
+arrays = {
+    name: np.load(io.BytesIO(base64.b64decode(value)))
+    for name, value in choice["flat_logprobs"].items()
+}
+sampled_logprobs = arrays["logprobs"][:, 0]  # one per generated token
+top_k_ids = arrays["token_ids"][:, 1:]
